what: The corrections ledger of the ω = 9/4 lane: every deviation from the pre-registration, read from corpus/omega-nine-fourths/DEVIATIONS.md, and every amendment, read from AMENDMENTS.md.

corrections.text: PREREG.md G6 says "28 compatibility patches"; lean/patches/ holds 27 patch files and a README. The PIN row found 0 of the 27 patched packages in the closure of the three theorems.

prompts/provenance-scout.md identified the paper's reference [41] as the two 2026-09-24 manuscripts. The scout (provenance/SCOUT.md) found [41] is the 2026-10-02 preprint "An Upper Bound of 9/4 for the Matrix Multiplication Exponent" (over ℂ); the two 2026-09-24 papers are [44] and [45].

G5 as sealed is a true sentence about DeepMind's notebook, but the scout reads it as stale: the upper bound ω ≤ 9/4 has seven outside write-ups (none refereed) and four outside Lean developments (three descend from OpenAI's October code; one, qit-lmu/omega, is code-independent and uses a rank-based ω). G5 stays listed, with this reading.

deviations.when: 2026-11-25 03:04 UTC, row PIN, script fix, no result changed
deviations.text: The first PIN run (03:02:16 UTC) cloned the release and printed its head as 92b516ef8e2abf66c3db7aa31438d3010bc7956f (runs/p1/pin-clone.txt), then stopped at 03:03:56 UTC on its own check "the release is not at 92b516ef": the check ran `git rev-parse` as root on a clone owned by the unprivileged user, and git refused the directory as of "dubious ownership", printing nothing. No file was checked and no sum written. The check now runs as the clone's owner (tools/runpod-omega-p1.sh); PIN is run again from the start.

deviations.when: 2026-11-25 03:07 UTC, row PIN, script fix before the seal, nothing sealed
deviations.text: The second PIN run finished at 03:06:18 UTC with a list of 11,278 files (sha256 064b658a…) that was NOT sealed, for two faults found on reading its log: one imported module, Lake.Util.Casing (imported by Mathlib.Tactic.Linter.TextBased), was left unresolved because the closure script searched the toolchain's src/lean but not src/lean/lake, where Lake's sources live; and the check of which compatibility patches touch closure files matched by path suffix only, so three paths inside other packages (e.g. PrimeNumberTheoremAnd/Erdos970/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Log/Basic.lean) were reported as Mathlib files. The script now also searches src/lean/lake and matches a patch's paths only inside the package the patch is named for. PIN is run a third time from the start; only that run's list is sealed (the unsealed one is kept in runs/p1/pin-attempt2/).

deviations.when: 2026-11-25 03:26 UTC, additions to Phase 1 at the control room's word; no pre-registered row changes
deviations.text: While K0 was building, the control room sent (a) the provenance scout's facts N1–N3 (AMENDMENTS.md A8) for CEN and the K0 log, and (b) the statement reader's decision tests for F4 (reader/tests at commit 94b626de: the six planted challenges V1–V6, each changing one definition body, which Comparator must refuse; the T3 pair ReaderDivision / ReaderDivisionPlanted, accept / refuse; T1–T5 with `lake env lean`) and its note on `rigidity` / `contact_of_installations`. These run AFTER the pre-registered rows, from a separate script (tools/runpod-omega-p1x.sh, which sources the running tools/runpod-omega-p1.sh unchanged; the running file is not edited). Two tests (T3_DivisionInEnv, T4) and N2 need two modules outside the sealed A1 closure (SpectralBooks.DivisionExponent and SpectralBooks.CircuitRankSpecialization); the files they add beyond A1, with the reader's test files, are hashed into A1x-SHA256SUMS and stamped (SEAL-A1x) before anything of them is built. Those two modules are then checked by Lean's kernel at build only (no Comparator config names them, no external kernel); this is said wherever their results are quoted.

deviations.when: 2026-11-25 04:19 UTC, row PIN's file list, found at CEN, no result changed
deviations.text: Lean imports `Init` implicitly into every file that does not begin with `prelude`; the PIN closure script read only the written `import` lines, so the sealed A1-target-SHA256SUMS lists 11,242 modules where the true import closure of the two modules has 11,337. The 95 missing are all toolchain files — Init.lean and 94 files under Init/ — from the official v4.34.1 archive, whose GitHub digest (47bf4bbd…) IS in A1, so their bytes were pinned before K0 through that digest, not file by file. With the implicit import added, the script's closure of {the solution module, Lean} equals, module for module, the 11,857 modules Lean's own environment reports in the census (CEN.out, CENIMP lines). The 95 files' sha256s are recorded in runs/p1/pod/x/init/missing-from-A1.SHA256SUMS (from the digest-checked archive). Found by the Phase 1 runner when the census compared Lean's import list with A1.

deviations.when: 2026-11-25 04:57 UTC, F4 test T2, a repair, not a finding
deviations.text: T2_AlphaOrientation.lean (reader/tests, 0a87a589…) did not elaborate on the pod (XT2, 04:53:39 UTC, exit 1): `readerRHS_swap13` (l.40–41) left the goal "unsolved" — the two sides differ only in how `max a 0 + max b 0 + max c 0` is bracketed, because the simp set had commutativity lemmas but no `add_assoc` (Lean also warned that `add_left_comm` was unused). The reader's file anticipates exactly this ("a tactic failure … repair … report it as a repair"). The statements and the three #print axioms lines are the reader's, unchanged. Run as XT2r1 with the same green rule.
